review_candidates.title: Client Relationship & Transactions Executive – Maritime, Yachting & Corporate
review_candidates.description: Client Relationship & Transactions Executive – Maritime, Yachting & Corporate MCConsult & Associates Ltd is seeking an experienced, highly organised and client-focused Client Relationship & Transactions Executive to join its team. This is a varied, hands-on position within a specialist maritime, shipping, yachting, legal and corporate services practice, supporting an international client base across corporate, commercial and maritime transactions. The role combines client relationship management with the administrative coordination and progression of transactions and client matters. The candidate will work closely with the firm's legal, corporate, compliance and maritime professionals, taking ownership of matters from an administrative and client-facing perspective and ensuring they progress efficiently from instruction through to completion. The candidate will deal directly with clients, government authorities and registries, banks and financiers, lawyers, accountants, auditors, notaries, corporate service providers, shipowners, managers and other professional advisers, both in Malta and internationally. Key Responsibilities The candidate's responsibilities will include: • Client & Matter Management – Acting as a key point of contact for clients; coordinating onboarding and internal handovers; managing client communications, requirements, deadlines and follow-ups; maintaining oversight of assigned matters; and assisting with matter administration and billing coordination. • Corporate & Maritime Transactions – Coordinating the administrative and client-facing aspects of corporate, commercial and maritime legal matters, including corporate formations and restructurings, ownership changes, vessel and yacht acquisitions and disposals, ship and yacht finance, mortgages and security transactions, share transfers and pledges, vessel registrations and other related transactions. • Transaction & Document Control – Coordinating documentation, corporate authorities, signature and execution processes, transaction checklists, closings and post-completion requirements; maintaining strict control of originals, certified/notarised documents, legalisations and apostilles; and ensuring documentation is properly logged, tracked, filed and safeguarded. • Authorities, Registries & Filings – Liaising with Maltese government authorities and registries, including the Malta Business Registry (MBR), Commissioner for Revenue (CFR) and Transport Malta; navigating relevant government portals; coordinating filings, registrations, searches and submissions; and actively following matters through to conclusion. • Resident Agent, AML/CFT & Sanctions Coordination – Assisting with relevant Resident Agent and sanctions-related matters; maintaining a good working knowledge of AML/CFT requirements applicable to client relationships and one-off transactions; liaising with clients regarding applicable requirements; and coordinating with the firm's legal or compliance professionals where substantive assessment or escalation is required. • Policies, Procedures & Internal Controls – Creating, maintaining and updating internal policies, procedures, transaction and onboarding checklists, workflows, templates, registers and trackers; identifying opportunities to improve administrative processes and document controls; and ensuring procedures remain current and consistently applied. • Data & Records Management – Maintaining accurate and up-to-date client, corporate, vessel and transaction data, together with complete and well-organised electronic and physical files, internal registers, databases and matter records. The Candidate The ideal candidate will have previous experience within a corporate, transactional, legal, maritime or professional services environment and a practical understanding of how professional transactions and client matters are administered. Previous experience with corporate transactions and documentation is important, while exposure to maritime, shipping or yachting matters will be considered a strong advantage. Practical experience dealing with Maltese government authorities and online portals, particularly the MBR and CFR, is important. Familiarity with Transport Malta and other maritime or regulatory authorities will be considered an advantage. The candidate should: • Be exceptionally organised, meticulous, proactive and reliable, with a strong sense of ownership and follow-through; • Be confident and professional in managing relationships with local and international clients, authorities and professional advisers; • Be capable of managing multiple transactions, clients, deadlines and priorities simultaneously; • Have practical knowledge of corporate and transactional documentation, execution formalities and administrative procedures; • Have a good working knowledge of AML/CFT requirements relevant to client relationships and one-off transactions, together with an understanding of sanctions requirements; • Be comfortable navigating government and regulatory procedures and following matters through to completion; • Have excellent written and spoken English and strong attention to detail; • Be capable of working independently while recognising when matters require professional review or escalation; and • Handle confidential client, corporate and transactional information with absolute discretion. Above all, the candidate should be someone who takes ownership of a matter and follows it through — keeping track of what is outstanding, following up proactively and ensuring that documentation, filings and administrative requirements are properly concluded. Why Join Us? This is not a conventional administrative position. The candidate will join a specialist maritime, shipping and yachting practice, gaining direct exposure to international clients and transactions involving vessels, yachts, corporate structures, ship finance, security arrangements, ownership transactions and cross-border commercial matters. The position offers the opportunity to develop into a central client relationship and transaction management role within a highly specialised international sector, working closely with legal, corporate, maritime and compliance professionals.

review_candidates.title: Butler
review_candidates.description: Company Description Raffles Hotels & Resorts The Birthplace of stories and legends since 1887, Raffles is a legendary brand, steeped in history and loved by generations past, present and future. Raffles, at distinguished landmark addresses around the world, is the vibrant heart of its destination, curating experiences that are culturally enriching, intellectually stimulating and always respectful of local communities, heritage and the environment. About Raffles The Palm Opened in 2021 on the western crescent of Palm Jumeirah, the world’s largest man-made island and archipelago, this palatial beach resort, featuring 340 spacious rooms, suites and villas, is inspired by the stunning elegance of European palaces and embellished with handcrafted Italian furniture. Guests can enjoy panoramic views, a private beach, state-of-the-art entertainment and recreational facilities, including specialist boutiques, a VIP movie theatre, and signature and private restaurants complemented by exquisite banqueting and conference spaces. More than a destination, Raffles the Palm Dubai embodies the spirit of a legendary brand, celebrated for its storied heritage since 1887 and its hallmark of intuitive, gracious service. At the palace, excellence is a craft, and every team member is a master in their field. Here, talent is not only recognized, it plays a vital role in shaping the next chapter of this extraordinary resort and its legacy within the brand. Job Description We invite you to join the world of luxury hospitality at Raffles The Palm as we currently looking for Butler. Reporting to the Butler Supervisor / Assistant Head Butler. The Raffles Butler is not defined by the tasks they perform, but by what they make possible for every guest they serve. This is a role of presence, not just procedure. The Butler is the architect of the individual guest journey: the single point of continuity from the moment a reservation is made to the moment a guest steps into the world again, and the reason they return. At Raffles, the Butler operates across two models of service. As Butler in Residence, they are a dedicated presence for every suite and VIP guest: proactive, personal, and fully accountable for the arc of that stay. As Butler on Call, they are a presence felt rather than seen: available, responsive, and ready to step in whenever a guest needs them. To the guest, both are simply 'The Butler.' Key Responsibilities Knowledge Hold thorough, practised knowledge of all Butler Service SOPs; not as rules to follow, but as a foundation from which to deliver with confidence and consistency. Remain fully current on Raffles Brand Standards, LQA criteria, Forbes Travel Guide standards, and the expectations that define five-star butler service globally. Maintain working proficiency across all platforms used to capture, action, and track the guest journey. Demonstrate accurate knowledge of all room categories, suite configurations, F&B offerings, in-house experiences, and property-wide facilities. Stay continuously informed on arriving guests: their profiles, histories, preferences, special occasions, and any intelligence gathered across all touchpoints. Remain current on local culture, seasonal events, and the area’s social landscape to serve as a credible and genuine resource for guests. The 360° Guest Journey Internalise and embody the Raffles brand personality in every interaction: Charming, Graceful, Thoughtful, and Welcoming. Consistently execute the Top 5 Service Excellence pillars in every guest encounter: Look, Smile, Talk, Listen, and Thank. Operate as the orchestrator of the guest journey; the conductor who ensures every department plays its part at precisely the right moment. Own the guest relationship from pre-arrival to post-departure, not as a series of handoffs, but as a single, unbroken arc of care. Initiate meaningful pre-arrival contact: review profiles with intent, anticipate what has not yet been asked for, and personalise every element of the arrival before the guest lands. Conduct in-room check-ins and room orientations with warmth and genuine curiosity; reading each guest to determine the level of engagement they seek. Correspond with guests via appropriate channels – written, digital, verbal – always in the Raffles tone: considered, elegant, and never transactional. Anticipate needs before they are expressed. A pattern observed becomes a gesture before departure. Be proactively present: visible, attuned, and ready throughout the entire stay. Manage all guest requests with full personal accountability; coordinating across departments, tracking to completion, and following up without being asked. Handle complaints and service failures with ownership and composure: acknowledge, recover, and follow through until the guest's trust is fully restored. Inspect arrival and occupied rooms through a butler's perspective. Execute Raffles Rituals and special occasion set-ups with precision, creativity, and genuine care for the detail. Offer packing and unpacking service with the discretion and attentiveness that transforms a practical task into a considered experience. Monitor DND and OOO rooms with diligence, acting on welfare concerns immediately and in full accordance with SOP. Maintain impeccable butler notes: recording preferences, observations, and interactions in a way that serves the next encounter as richly as the current one. Practise genuine, knowledgeable upselling; recommending experiences, dining, and services because they are right for this guest, not to meet a metric. Collaborate daily with Housekeeping, Private Dining, Front Office, Engineering, Concierge, and all relevant departments; communicating with clarity, respect, and shared ownership of the guest outcome. Embody the 'We Are All Butlers' philosophy: treat every colleague as a contributor to the guest journey, and every interaction – internal or external – as a reflection of the Raffles standard. Attend shift briefings, department meetings, and training sessions with active engagement. Contribute to the team's culture through reliability, discretion, and a consistent willingness to support colleagues. Qualifications PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES Guest Journey Ownership, Empathy & Anticipation, Emotional Intelligence, Personalisation, Cultural Sensitivity, Service Recovery, Attention to Detail, Multitasking, Strong Interpersonal Skills Commercial awareness. review_candidates.description: Hertfordshire Constabulary Police Staff Permanent Full Time ICT Headquarters, Huntingdon, Cambs , Headquarters, WGC, Herts A4 £32,613 37 A great opportunity has arisen to join a growing support team as an ICT Senior Service Desk Analyst within the BCH (Beds, Cambs & Herts) ICT Department. Join the exciting and dynamic world of policing and contribute towards making Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire a safer place. Based at Hertfordshire Constabulary HQ or Cambridgeshire Constabulary, you will play a key role within the ICT Operations Team, supporting the tri-force ICT estate and ensuring that vital business systems remain highly available to officers and staff. About The Role As a Senior Service Desk Analyst, you will provide first-line ICT support while also taking on additional responsibility for supporting and guiding a team of five analysts. You will act as an escalation point for more complex or non-standard issues, helping to drive service quality and improve first-time fix rates. You will use your technical knowledge and customer service skills to diagnose hardware, software and communication issues reported via phone or self-service. Where resolution is not possible at first contact, you will ensure incidents are accurately logged, fully documented, and escalated within agreed SLAs, maintaining clear communication with users throughout. You will also contribute to continuous improvement by maintaining knowledge base articles and coaching the development of colleagues across the Service Desk. Why Join BCH ICT? Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Police form one of the largest and most established collaborations in the UK. This role offers a fantastic opportunity to develop your career within a supportive and forward-thinking ICT environment, with exposure to a diverse technology estate and opportunities to build leadership experience. Employee Benefits 25 days annual leave, rising to 29 after 5 years’ service (plus public holidays) Competitive Local Government Pension Scheme Access to on-site gym facilities at HQ locations Hybrid working arrangements Blue Light Card discounts Sports and social club membership Employee Assistance Programme Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Everyone at Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire takes personal responsibility to help create an inclusive workplace, where police officers and staff respect one another, feel valued for their differences and can be themselves. We are committed to providing reasonable adjustments, wherever needed so everyone feels welcome and can flourish. We are working hard to continue to enhance and increase our diversity across the three forces, where communities are under-represented, including those from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities, people of all ages, abilities, faiths, religions and gender, LGBT communities and those from other disadvantaged or marginalised backgrounds, who share our values and wish to make a difference to the communities we serve. All applications will be treated on merit, based on the evidence provided in your application and your suitability for the role for which you have applied. We are a Disability Confident employer offering a guaranteed interview scheme for all candidates with a disability covered by the Equality Act 2010 who meet the minimum entry requirements. Should you require any reasonable adjustments for your application process, please contact the HR Recruitment Centre on 01438 757 777. Flexible Working BCH supports agile and flexible working wherever possible. All requests will be considered in line with operational requirements. Police Barred and Advisory lists Individuals placed on the Police Barred and Advisory lists will not be considered for employment by the police for a minimum of 5 years from the date of listing in the case of gross misconduct, or 3 years from the date of listing in the case of poor performance. Vetting and Safeguarding BCH are committed to safeguarding and operate safer recruitment processes, to ensure a police service that employees are proud to work for because they feel safe, valued and part of a happy and supportive work environment. All employees and volunteers therefore will be subject to background checks including vetting and references. Please be aware the Police Corporate Vetting Unit will undertake security vetting on successful candidates, their family and others that live at their home address, which will include financial checks. How To Apply If you are successful, you will be joining one of the most accomplished policing collaborations in the UK where our vision for the future of BCH Policing is exhibited daily across the full breadth of capabilities and functions we deliver. Please Submit Your CV Along With Evidence of your relevant skills and experience A 500-word statement demonstrating how you meet the minimum entry requirements For further information, please contact Jamie Read (BCH Operations, ICT Service Desk Team Leader) via Jamie.Read@cambs.police.uk Additional Advert Information Internal Applicants To apply for this role, internal applicants must have successfully completed their probationary period. If you qualify as an internal candidate within the advertising force, you may upload either your CV or the internal role summary form attached to this advert. Vetting Process Please note that, as part of the vetting process, the BCH Vetting Unit may need to contact your current line manager for a Supervisor Appraisal. This requirement aligns with the 2025 National Guidelines for Vetting (APP 6.5.18). Examples Of When This May Apply Include Transferring to another force Renewing vetting clearance Moving into a role requiring MV clearance (even if you currently hold MV clearance) Moving into or working in a role involving close contact with vulnerable individuals If any of the above apply to you, please expect your line manager to be contacted when you submit your vetting application. Redeployment and Redundancy This vacancy is open to employees at risk of redundancy and will remain available to redeployees until a final offer has been agreed and accepted. Redeployees at risk of redundancy will take priority over all other applicants at any stage of the recruitment process. If successful, redeployees will remain on their home force’s terms and conditions. Role Profile We recommend downloading and saving a copy of the role profile, as it will no longer be accessible once the advert closes. Commitment to Inclusion As a Disability Confident Leader, we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued, and able to be themselves. We provide workplace adjustments wherever needed so that all colleagues can thrive. If you have a disability and meet the minimum criteria for the role, you will be guaranteed an interview under the Offer an Interview Scheme.

Since launch, the company has supported more than 80 clients across varied industries, focusing on quality, speed, and competitive pricing. Role Description This is a full-time Financial Analysis & Accounting role for a French-speaking professional, based in Giza with a hybrid work arrangement that allows some work from home. The role involves preparing and analyzing financial statements, monitoring budgets, and performing variance analyses to support decision-making. Daily tasks include handling accounting entries, reconciliations, and month-end closing activities, while ensuring compliance with relevant financial standards and internal policies. The position also includes conducting market and financial research, preparing reports and presentations in French and English, and communicating findings to internal stakeholders and clients. The individual will collaborate with cross-functional teams, support audits, and contribute to continuous improvement of financial processes and controls. Qualifications Strong Analytical Skills and Finance knowledge to perform financial modeling, budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis. Effective Communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear financial reports and explain findings to non-financial stakeholders. Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken, with the ability to handle financial documentation and client communication in both languages. Solid understanding of accounting principles, financial controls, and reporting standards; experience with accounting software and advanced Excel skills. Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; relevant professional certifications (e.g., CMA, CPA) are an advantage. Detail-oriented, organized, and able to manage multiple deadlines in a hybrid work environment, demonstrating reliability and integrity. Prior experience in financial analysis, accounting, or consulting in a multinational or client-focused setting is preferred.
